paper_metadata.title: Slip-band-driven dynamic recrystallization mediated strain hardening in HfNbTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibit outstanding strength at room temperature, but their high-temperature applications are hindered by severe strain-softening.
Here, we report slip-band-driven dynamic recrystallization to enhance the high-temperature strain hardening of HfNbTaTiZr RHEA.

other.remelting_cycles: no less than four additional remelting cycles

evidence.quote: Initially, ingots weighing approximately 40 g each were meticulously crafted by subjecting a blend of exceptionally pure metals (with a minimum purity of 99.95 %) to arc-melting, maintaining specific molar ratios. To ensure optimal chemical uniformity, these initial ingots underwent no less than four additional remelting cycles within an environment of high-purity argon, employing a Ti-gettering technique.

Subsequently, a batch of tens ingots was subjected to cold crucible induction levitation melting within an argon-filled atmosphere, yielding a larger primary billet measuring around 40 mm in diameter and approximately 31 mm in thickness.

To enhance the initial grain structure, a high-temperature forging technique was employed, involving multiple orientations applied to the primary billet. The process commenced with heating the primary billet to 1000 °C, followed by an isothermal multi-directional forging. The subsequent step involved air cooling, ultimately resulting in the attainment of a final thickness measuring approximately 15 mm. This thickness was achieved through a reduction rate of approximately 52 %.

Dog-bone-shaped specimens with pin-loaded ends were meticulously fashioned by electrical discharge wire-cutting for tension assessments in adherence to ASTM E8M-09. These specimens exhibited dimensions of 14 mm in gage length, 3.5 mm in width, and 1.5 mm in thickness.
